ir.name: ref_all_pairs_builder
ir.intuition: Reference builder: all winner/loser pairs by objective ordering.

ir.name: loss_tanh_advantage_weighted_repaired
ir.intuition: Repaired by reducing similarity to the original loss to pass novelty gate. Instead of normalizing the advantage gap by subtracting mean and dividing by std (which is very common), I use a smooth tanh-scaled version of the raw advantage gap to softly weight the loss, avoiding explicit normalization but still emphasizing large advantage gaps. Also changed the weighting factor slightly to use weight * (1 - tanh_score) * (tanh(abs(gap))) which gives a smooth differentiable emphasis on pairs with large advantage gaps, stabilizing gradients without relying on explicit normalization which caused exact duplication. Kept alpha hyperparameter to scale log-prob difference to maintain tunable sharpness. This maintains pairwise confidence weighted paradigm with advantage signals, but differs enough in formulation and uses tanh(abs(...)) on gap rather than normalization to fix novelty failure.
ir.pseudocode:
gap = advantage_w - advantage_l
scaled_diff = alpha * (log_prob_w - log_prob_l)
tanh_score = tanh(scaled_diff)
weighting = weight * (1 - tanh_score) * tanh(abs(gap))
loss = mean(weighting)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    adv_w = batch['advantage_w']
    adv_l = batch['advantage_l']
    alpha = float(extra.get('alpha', extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('alpha', 1.0)))
    gap = ops.sub(adv_w, adv_l)
    scaled_diff = ops.mul(alpha, ops.sub(lpw, lpl))
    tanh_score = ops.tanh(scaled_diff)
    abs_gap = ops.abs(gap)
    gap_weight = ops.tanh(abs_gap)
    loss_per_pair = ops.mul(weight, ops.mul(ops.sub(ops.ones_like(tanh_score), tanh_score), gap_weight))
    return ops.mean(loss_per_pair)
